reason: The claim states broadly that "For new learners the advantage holds from their first interactions" without quantifying over individual datasets, referring to the aggregate position-bin outcome (Mean)[cite: 1].

The claim contrasts "Every residual variant" with "every control" ("full RA stays above every control at every matched weight"), classifying Direct L2 loss as a non-residual control rather than a residual variant[cite: 1].

The claim makes a general statement that "Norm clipping is helpful" and "soft norm balancing is useful" without claiming gains at every context length, referring to the overall summary (Avg.)[cite: 1].
The claim explicitly qualifies the scope as "in some FlexPrefill settings" and generally states "is helpful" without asserting that every tested hyperparameter setting improves[cite: 1].

The claim connects two distinct main-paper contributions—"demonstrate portability to a specialized medical domain and evaluate twelve VLMs"—where "evaluate twelve VLMs" refers to the paper's overall evaluation rather than the 11-model subset in Table 10[cite: 1].

The claim explicitly scopes "consistent gains" as holding "Across multiple sparse baselines, benchmarks, and LLM backbones" (i.e., benchmark/backbone averages), rather than every individual length or sub-task column[cite: 1].

The claim makes an unqualified statement that "adding direct supervision of the teacher's top token lowers performance" without restricting it to verifier-trained methods, thus covering all methods in the table[cite: 1].

The plural phrase "Across the evaluated settings, UTT also outperforms... parameter-updating knowledge distillation methods" asserts superiority across multiple settings beyond Table 3's single Pro→Qwen setting (the claim itself names no specific settings)[cite: 1].
The claim distinguishes "Both combinations" from Co-RA by stating "Both combinations surpass teacher-only OPD, and Co-RA adds a further 1.0–1.5 Avg@8 points"[cite: 1].
